name: POST /api/leadflow/meetings/{id}/rescue-call - Log the human call that unlocks the rescue
description: Records that a rep called the contact after a no-show, which is the precondition POST /api/leadflow/meetings/{id}/rescue refuses without. THE ORDER IS THE RULE: a rescue message sent before anybody picked up the phone is automation talking over a person who has just missed a meeting, so the call is logged first and the rescue is permitted second. 200 rather than 201 - it stamps the existing no-show record. Both stamps use COALESCE, so logging a second call does not overwrite the first: the question the record answers is when the FIRST human contact happened, and a later retry must not move it. attempt_id is optional and links the log to a specific call attempt when the telephony connector produced one. QA: depends on POST /api/leadflow/meetings and POST /api/leadflow/meetings/{id}/no-show - there is no no-show record to stamp until the meeting has been marked missed, which is why that definition needed a happy path before this one could exist.

testCases.name: The human call is logged and the rescue becomes permitted
NEGATIVE: a meeting with no no-show recorded against it
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all

errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, or present without a bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired

no no-show is recorded for that meeting. Refused rather than created, because a rescue call logged against a meeting nobody missed would unlock a rescue message for a customer who is still expecting the original.
